description:
Make `jit validate --fix` derive every fix from one captured validation, publish them in one mutation, and always render the one report computed over the fixed repository.

## Background

- `validate_with_fix` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:42-97`) first runs a full validation whose result fix mode discards (`:44`), then publishes each hierarchy type fix (`detect_and_fix_hierarchy_issues` `:1140-1216`, `apply_type_fix` `:1218-1234`, reading the hierarchy and issue list from disk), the transitive reduction (`reduce_all_dependencies`, already one mutation), each readiness correction in up to ten passes (`check_pending_transitions` `:2081-2137`, one lifecycle mutation per correction through `auto_transition_to_ready` and `auto_transition_to_backlog`, `commands/issue.rs:817,834`) and the derived-state repair (`repair_derived_state` (`commands/validate.rs:599-643`), one mutation). It re-validates only when it applied a fix, so a zero-fix run over an index that disagrees with the issue files prints "No fixes needed" and exits 0 while plain `jit validate` fails.
- `auto_transition_to_backlog` has no other caller; `auto_transition_to_ready` is also called at `commands/issue.rs:873`.
- Pure derivations exist: `generate_fixes` over `detect_validation_issues` (`domain::type_taxonomy`), `derive_dependency_repair` (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:854`, private), `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` (`domain/types.rs`), and `derive_materialization` for derived state. `finalize` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:719`) turns issue intents into a plan, and `RepositoryDelta::new` (`repository_state/image.rs:1239-1256`) accepts concatenated actions and refuses duplicate targets.
- `test_apply_type_fix_preserves_concurrent_type_correction` (`commands/validate.rs:2874`) shows that a type correction saved between capture and apply survives.
- The `--fix` branch of the `Commands::Validate` arm in `main.rs`, which calls `validate_with_fix`, renders `{valid, fixes_applied, dry_run, message}` in JSON. `jit recover` calls `repair_derived_state` (`commands/claim.rs:733`) and keeps doing so.

Kept as one change for a build reason: the fix return value and its renderer compile only together.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `--fix` computes no report before deriving its fixes. It derives the hierarchy, reduction, readiness and derived-state fixes from one validation capture, folding the issue edits per issue, and publishes them all through one mutation; `--dry-run` derives the same plan and publishes nothing; when the captured records do not parse, no fix is derived and the post-fix report carries the structural failure.
- [hard] REQ-02: Readiness corrections apply `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` to the projected issue set until none remains, and no other readiness derivation is introduced; `detect_and_fix_hierarchy_issues`, `apply_type_fix`, `check_pending_transitions` and `auto_transition_to_backlog` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: `--fix` always computes one report over the repository as the fixes leave it, including when it applied none, and renders it as plain `jit validate` does, with the fix count and messages; its exit status follows that report. A harness test shows one publication carrying fixes of every class, and a CLI test over an index that disagrees with the issue files shows `--fix` failing as plain `validate` does, which fails on today's code.
- [hard] REQ-04: A harness test replaces `test_apply_type_fix_preserves_concurrent_type_correction`: a type correction saved between capture and publish survives the composed fix, which re-derives over the new state. The listed fix suites pass with their assertions on repository state unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour and output change: `--fix --json` carries the post-fix report fields and its exit status follows that report.
- A later pure readiness derivation that every mutation shares will replace the fixpoint loop in this change.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: One mutation and one post-fix report for validate --fix
